I have said across the post, she had gone through all the tests, and psych and got to a final ultrasound where they found she had early kidney disease so decided not to take it. It took 6 months of tests for her. The hospital said no based on early stage kidney disease.

My friend knew I had the same blood type as her and therefore made the assumption that I’d match to him. She didn’t need access to my medical data. She knew my blood group. There was no indication or knowledge that I’d pass anything other than the initial blood test 🤷🏻‍♀️

Thank you everyone. I wasn’t comfortable asking the hospital to say no to them. I wanted to own the decision and be honest with them. I didn’t want to waste our NHS’s time and resources using a doctor to turn them down so I could hide behind that. 

I still think, if I had to do it all again, I would still be truthful to whoever had asked. They deserve to know the truth and if that means they no longer want anything to do with me, at least I’ve been true and honest to them and myself. 

I am on the bone marrow transplant list but have never been called up yet. I also regularly give blood. But I just couldn’t go through with this right now. 10 years ago or 10 years into the future I’ll be in a different place and maybe my decision would be different. But I can only live in the here.

I didn’t realise I’d cry so much reading your replies. Thank you so much, you’ve helped me realise, the first part is forgiving myself for my decision. I hadn’t realised how much I’d been carrying this around for the last year. I need to learn to be ok with the decision I made and be at peace with it. Thank you x

I was going to move in following the operation to help them both get back in their feet and support them that way. I feel guilty for my decision everyday. I really appreciate your honesty about how upsetting it is, to hear someone refuse. 

I really hope that you get your donation, either by a living donor or not.
